beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Dhruvi Mehta, an international master's student in Information Systems at Northeastern. My final project is Ghost-Job Trust Radar: it checks whether a job ad is still real and fits a student's visa timeline, before they spend time on it. If something already ran, I'll show it. Everything else is a plan.

beats.narration_text: Four terms. CPT: permission for an international student to work during their degree. A ghost job: an ad that's already filled, or never really open. Liveness: is the ad still taking applications? A sponsor record: proof a company sponsored work visas before.

beats.narration_text: An international student on CPT finds a data analyst posting and spends an hour researching the company. Then she learns it was already filled, or the start date doesn't fit her CPT window. That hour is gone.

beats.narration_text: Ghost-Job Trust Radar will be a command-line tool: one command, three checks, like a checkpoint for a job ad. Is it open? Does the timeline fit CPT? Has the company sponsored before? It will live in a GitHub repository with tests and an evaluation log.

beats.narration_text: I checked two alternatives myself. On MyVisaJobs, Stripe appears under four company names, and nothing says whether a posting is still open. Checking one posting by hand took me three tabs and twenty minutes, and left no record except my own screenshots.

beats.narration_text: Mine will ask the cheapest question first: is the ad still open? I already ran my class engine's live check on a real Stripe posting, and it came back active. A made-up job number came back 'uncertain', not 'dead', so anything except 'active' will stop the check.

beats.narration_text: Here's what exists. I built two scripts: one checks the visa timeline, one pulls sponsorship history from the class data. Sixteen automatic tests pass, and I checked one run by hand against the raw data.
beats.motion_claim: REAL. The lens moves down the two real test lines from the 2026-10-10 run to the total, 16.

beats.narration_text: Then I tried to break it, with a company that isn't in the dataset. It reported 'no record' instead of inventing an answer.

beats.narration_text: What does this prove? Four course skills: checking results against the source, labeling where answers came from, testing how it fails, and writing rules it must follow. A reviewer could say my checks fail safely, but not yet that it's accurate on real postings.

beats.narration_text: What's out: it won't say whether to apply, or give legal advice, and it doesn't read experience levels yet; the Stripe posting I tested asks for six-plus years. First, one command will run every check on a synthetic posting and save a report, a test, and a dated run log.

beats.narration_text: The biggest risk: the sponsorship data is an incomplete, historical sample, so 'no record' could be misread as 'doesn't sponsor.' Every lookup will print the data's date range next to the answer.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a problem I live with as an international student. Python and data cleaning I already have, with my scripts as evidence; prompt contracts and evaluation logs are new to me.

beats.narration_text: So, where things stand. Today: two scripts, sixteen passing tests, a break test, and one live check on a real posting, in an open pull request. Still to build: one command, name matching, and an evaluation log. This film doesn't show it works on real postings in general.
beats.motion_claim: CONSTRUCTED. The tab switches from what exists today to what will exist.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Before researching your next posting: is it still accepting applications, and does the start date fit your work window? Note where each answer came from.
